text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- President Jacques Chirac and Chancellor Helmut Kohl progress toward an agreement on future European monetary stability pact.
-- Paris bourse flirts with record highs.
-- Eurotunnel wins approval from intergovernmental safety committee to resume partial passenger service in Channel tunnel.
-- Paribas subsidiary Compagnie Bancaire forecasts a 1.2 billion francs loss for 1996.
-- Bomb blast killed two, injures 83 in Paris suburban train last night.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Finance minister Jean Arthuis says surprised that banking watchdog continuing to allow property bank Credit Foncier to continue to lend as union protestors invade board meeting Tuesday.
-- CFDT labour union alleges that a planned Thomson privatisation contains illegal aspects, notably in the fact that Thomson and Thomson Multimedia are to be sold separately.
-- RPR Gaullist party parliamentarians opposed to a cut in wealth tax increased last year by the government.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Boeing chairman Ronald Woodard in an interview says planned co-operation with McDonnell-Douglas on civilian aircraft and notably extended versions of the 747 will improve competitivity.
-- CIC chairman Bernard Yoncourt resigns, is expected to be replaced by Philippe Pontet.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- President Jacques Chirac and Chancellor Helmut Kohl vow to make a success of a European summit meeting in Dublin next week.
-- Strike to carry on today at EDF-GDF electricity and gas suppliers against planned energy markets deregulation.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Turmoil ahead for Europe as it progresses toward a single currency amid strikes, social unrest, and arms-wrestling between France and Germany over ways to guarantee fiscal discipline.
